findings.title: Gaza Civil Defence reports roughly 1,500 storm distress calls in 10 hours, rescues residents from partially collapsed Nuseirat building and warns of insufficient shelter and rescue resources
findings.publisher: Al Jazeera, reporting direct statements by Gaza Civil Defence; 1,500-call total also reported by Kuwait Times/KUNA
findings.event_period: 10 hours after storm began early Saturday 7 November 2026; exact beginning/end hours not verified
findings.location: Gaza Strip, including Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza, displacement shelters across multiple Gaza governorates
findings.affected_population_system: Displaced Palestinian families, emergency callers, occupants of a partially collapsed building and Gaza Civil Defence emergency response/shelter capacity
findings.exact_supporting_passage: Gaza’s civil defence agency said its crews received about 1,500 distress calls in just 10 hours
findings.confidence_basis: Al Jazeera directly quotes spokesperson Mahmoud Basal and Gaza Civil Defence leadership; independent Al Jazeera Arabic report carries same 1,500-call number and Nuseirat evacuation; media accounts rely substantially on the same Civil Defence statements, so not independent incident verification.
findings.bounded_discovery_context: The prior verified Gaza heartbeat already recorded November 7 flooding and two northern Gaza wall-collapse injuries as duplicates; this watch adds a traceable Civil Defence emergency-response burden, reported 30–40cm inundation at some shelters, new Nuseirat building-evacuation account and its stated inability to provide replacement shelter. Al Jazeera article dated Nov 7, with a syndication/index timestamp potentially before this observation window; discovery is new-to-watch, not proof all calls/evacuations occurred during this hour. No independent count verification. Excludes uncorroborated 70,000-flooded-tents estimate.
